narrative.title: Reconciling Two Ledger Entries
narrative.scenario: A reconciliation job receives one batch of transaction amounts and a settlement figure, and exactly one pair of amounts in the batch adds up to that figure. Auditors need the positions of the two entries rather than their values. Each entry may be used at most once, and the pair may be reported in any order.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers and an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: Two distinct 0-indexed positions i and j with i != j such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target, in any order.

testCases.explanation: Positions 0 and 1 hold 2 and 7, which sum to the settlement figure 9.
The matching entries sit at positions 1 and 2; the leading 3 is not part of the pair.

hintLevels: Level 1: For each entry, the partner you need is fully determined - it is the settlement figure minus that entry.
Level 2: Record each value against its position as you sweep the batch, then ask the table whether the needed partner has already been seen.
Level 3: Store the position only after the lookup so a single entry is never paired with itself, and remember a value may legitimately repeat in two different positions.
